caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 383 of 1996
lawyer:
Mr. Manzurur Rahim with Ms. Afreen Mahiuddin and Mr. AHM Mushfiqur Rahman, Advocates ------- for appellants.
Mr. Amir-U1-Islam with Mr. Rabi Shanker Chakraborty and Mr. Manzil Mursed, Advocates ------ for respondent No. 1
parties:
M/s. Bangladesh General Insurance Co. Ltd. ------- Appellants
Vs.
M/s. Meghna Sea Foods Ltd. ------- Respondent
full_judgment:
Md Tafazzul Islam, J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 18.9.96 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong in Money Suit No. 35 of 1992 decreeing the suit. 

 2. The respondents as plaintiffs, filed the above money suit praying for decree of Tk. 77,40,092/- against the defendant-appellants stating inter alia that they are engaged in export of frozen shrimps, white fish, frog legs etc and their fish processing factory and cold storage situated at BFDC Industrial Area, Tackpara, Cox's Bazar consists of usual fish receiving and processing room, chill room, ice making plant quick freezing and packing, two cold storage chambers were fish and frog legs are stored between 18'C to 20'c, compressors, transformer, amonia condensers and disel generators etc. which are insured with the defendants, defendant No. 1 being the group leader and the defendant No. 2,3,4 and 5 being the Co-Insurers and Share Holder of MBP (Machinery Breakdown) Policy being No. BGIC/CTG/KG. MBD/P. 01 12/90 and ENDT No. BGIC/CTG/KG/MBD/ENDT/OI-01/91 I(Co Insc) for Tk. 1,61,00,000/- covering risk of machinery breakdown between the period from 31.12.90 to 31.12.91. Further the stock of Shrimps frog legs and other white fish were also covered against deterioration following machinery break down under DOS (Deterioration of stock) Policy being No. BIGC/CM/ KG/DOS/P-01/12/90 (Co Insc) convering the same period and total sum insured was Tk. 6,30,00,000/- on standard terms and condition and also the exclusions as mentioned in the policy. As per terms and condition laid down in ENDT No. 903 which has been attached to it, this DOS policy has been extended to cover the risk of deterioration or putrefaction occurring as a result of failure of public power supply on 29.4.91 at about 17.15 hours, the industrial power feeder to the aforesaid BFDC Industrial Estate failed and was not restored until 19 hours on 4.5.91. 

 3. Is the plaintiff entitled to a decree as prayed for? 

 4. What relief if by the plaintiff entitled to decree as prayed for? 

 6. The learned Subordinate Judge after hearing the parties decreed the suit holding that insurance is co-operative device to spread the loss caused by a particular peril over a number of persons who are exposed to it and agree to ensure themselves against that risk and the insurance policy is the evidence of such device. The risk has increased, so the periferry of insurable interest on multi folded. DOS policy is under the General Insurance Branch of miscellaneous category where under taking to power supply was given and in the endorsement 903, the disruption of power supply due to Act of God being not specifically Endorsed, the Endorsement No. 903 is subject exclusion No. 7(d), if the public power supply failed due to cyclone. But since the factory situated at Cox's Bazar which is cyclone belt and the risk involved is with reference to the given circumstances of the locality and since the defendants were well aware that the fish plant is dependent on public electric supply and the fact is that the power supply did not stop before the cyclone came and moreover cyclone is quite normal in Cox's. Bazar and that the defence of exclusion of cyclone as a direct cause of deterioration is not established here as the case is that the damage was caused due to power failure and the power failed due to cyclone and so the inflict of cyclone is one of the causes proximate and so the insurance is bound' recognise the peril and is liable to indemnify the plaintiff. The learned Subordinate Judge held that the whole scheme of the insurance policy would be meaningless if the Court is lead to read some indirect or remote causes or events apart from their strict terms of the endorsement in the DOS policy. 

 9. Heard the leaned Advocate and perused the contents of the impugned judgment and decree and the depositions and the exhibits. As it appears the plaintiff examined 4 witnesses to prove their case P.W.1 who is the manager of the plaintiff, in his deposition more or less stated reiterated the plaint case. He proved Ext. 1 the DOS policy with Endorsement No. 903 Ext. 1 (ka) the MBD policy, Ext. 1 (Kha) letter of Endorsement dated 20.1.91 as contained in MBD policy. Ext. 2 receipt of premium dated 20.1.91 against. MBD policy. Ext. 3(Ka) and 3(kha) letters of defendant No. 1 dated 6.5.91 and 11.5.91 to the plaintiff. Ext. 3(Ga) letter dated 2.8.91 dated of Allied Inspection Company, the Surveyor P.W. 2, who is the factory manager of the plaintiff company, in his deposition also more or less reiterated the plaint case. He also proved Ext. 1(ka) i.e., "DOS policy with Endorsement No. 903, Ext 1(ka) the MBD policy, Ext. 1 (Kha) letter of Endorsement dated 20.1.91 as contained of MBD policy Ext. 2. receipt of premium dated 20.1.91 against MBD policy. Ext. 3(Ka) and 2(Kha) letters of defendant No. 1 dated 6.5.91 and 11.5.91 to the plaintiff, Ext. 3(Ga) letter dated 2.8.91 of Allied Inspection Company to the Surveyor. P.W.3 is the Inspector of Fish Inspection and Quality Control Department and proved Ext. 5, and 7(kha) are the same test report dated 8.5.91 regarding the conditions of frozen fish which he gave after inspection P.W. 4 is the Sub Divisional Engineer BDB Cox's Bazar who proved Ext. 8 the certificate dated 12.5.91 given by him on behalf of Executive Engineer Cox's Bazar. 

 31. It appears that the learned Subordinate Judge without considering the actually issue in matters decreed the suit on extraneous grounds holding that the Insurance. Policy covered even cyclone as in Cox's Bazar region, cyclone are frequent and what was the requirement for the plaintiff to make only any insurance if cyclone was kept outside the cover of the policy and claims due to cyclone are not entertained. Further the learned Sub-ordinate Judge failed to consider that detoriation was caused due to direct and indirect effect of cyclone. 

 32. In view of the above, we are of the view that the learned Subordinate Judge acted illegally in decreeing the suit and so the impugned judgment and decree cannot be sustained. 

 33. In the result, the appeal is allowed without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 12.9.96 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong in Money Suit No. 35 of 1992 is set aside and the suit filed by the plaintiff respondent is dismissed.
